Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your little one has arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days, and it helps us see whether you might benefit from a little extra emotional support or resources. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell us someone is in danger. We’ll go at your pace, and there are no right or wrong answers. Ready to start?

First question:  
Over the past week, have you been able to enjoy things as much as you usually do, or has pleasure felt harder to find?

I guess I do still enjoy some things—like when the baby smiles or when I get to take a short walk—but it doesn’t feel quite the same as before. It’s like the happiness is there, just a little dimmer, if that makes sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I can still laugh sometimes—like when my partner makes a silly joke or when the dog does something goofy—but I don’t find myself chuckling as easily or as often as I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like my mom coming over or a quiet cup of coffee—but the excitement feels kind of muted. It’s more “that’ll be nice” than the bubbly, can’t-wait feeling I used to have.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was fussy and I kept thinking maybe I’m not feeding him right or I did something to upset him. I know rationally it’s not my fault, but the thought still pops in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just be sitting there and suddenly worry that the baby’s breathing has changed or that I missed a wet diaper, even though he’s fine. It’s quick—I can usually talk myself down—but it happens a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky, but once or twice I’ve had this sudden rush of “what if I’m not doing enough?” and my heart speeds up for a minute. It passes pretty fast, though; I haven’t had a full-blown panic feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me
Some days, yeah. Like when the laundry piles up or the baby won’t settle, I feel a wave of “I can’t keep up.” I usually manage to push through, but it feels heavier than it used to.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, nothing that bad. I do have nights where it takes me a while to fall asleep—my mind keeps going over the day—but once I’m out, I stay asleep. I wouldn’t say I’m lying there miserable, just a little restless.
I have felt sad or miserable
I get moments—maybe once a day—where I just feel kind of down, like a cloud passing over. It’s not all day, and I can still smile when the baby coos, but the sad feeling pops up more than it used to.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, that’s happened a couple of times this week. Once was when the baby wouldn’t nap and I just felt overwhelmed, and another time was after a phone call with my mom—nothing major, just suddenly teary.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, not at all. I’ve never had anything like that cross my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Presenting symptoms  
- Mild anhedonia (reduced laughter, muted excitement)  
- Daily transient low mood (“cloud” episodes)  
- Two crying spells this week related to feeling overwhelmed  
- Self-blame/guilt when infant fussy  
- Intermittent, self-limited anxious worries (baby’s breathing, “doing enough”) with brief heart racing; no full panic  
- Occasional “things getting on top of me”; pushes through  
- Initial insomnia ruminating about the day; no middle/late insomnia; no suicidal ideation  

Pattern  
Persistent mild-moderate mood and anxiety symptoms, situational tearfulness, intact reality testing and safety.  

Screening significance  
Meets some criteria for minor postpartum depression and/or Generalized Anxiety Disorder, but does not endorse severe impairment, hopelessness, or self-harm. Continue monitoring, consider formal assessment with EPDS/PHQ-9 and clinical interview.
